Highly Enantioselective Construction of Fully Substituted
Stereocenters Enabled by In Situ Phosphonium-Containing
Organocatalysis
Hongkui Zhang, § Chunhui Jiang, § Jian-Ping Tan, Hui-Lin Hu, Yayun Chen, Xiaoyu Ren,
Hong-Su Zhang, and Tianli Wang *
Cite This: ACS Catal. 2020, 10, 5698 −5706 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: We present, herein, an important and practical class of
bifunctional in situ phosphonium-containing organocatalysis and its initial
application in highly e ﬃcient and enantioselective construction of N-
containing fully substituted stereocenters through an asymmetric decarbox-
ylative transformation between cyclic ketimines and β-keto acids. With this
catalytic protocol, a variety of optically active cyclic tertiary amine derivatives
were readily synthesized in high yields with excellent enantioselectivities
(99.0 to >99.9% ee) under very low catalyst loading (0.5 mol %). The success
of gram-level preparation and synthetic transformations proves the potential
of this catalytic strategy for practical applications. Mechanistic investigation,
including control experiments, in situ NMR analysis, and ESI-HRMS
characterization of intermediates, provides insights into the mechanism.
KEYWORDS: fully-substituted stereocenter, decarboxylative addition, phosphine-allenoate organocatalysis, Brønsted base,
reaction mechanism
■ INTRODUCTION
Over the past decades, nucleophilic organophosphine catalysis
has emerged as a powerful approach for the creation of
structurally diverse and synthetically valuable chiral molecules
in organic chemistry.
1,2 In general, phosphine-directed catalytic
events typically started with nucleophilic addition of a tertiary
phosphine catalyst to an electron-de ﬁcient reactant such as
alkene, allene, and alkyne, forming the key zwitterionic
intermediate which can further react with a variety of
electrophilic reactants to furnish di ﬀerent enantioselective
chemical transformations.
2 Notably, such zwitterion inter-
mediates generated upon phosphine addition are basic in
nature
3−5 and can thus be utilized as a new class of organic
base catalysts in asymmetric synthesis. Accordingly, phosphine-
containing Brønsted base catalysis has recently been
developed. As a particularly successful motif, Zhao and co-
workers introduced their pioneering investigations on
phosphine-acrylate dual-rea gent catalysis using Mannich-
type
6a−f and Strecker 6g reactions for de ﬁning the state of this
art, in which the zwitterionic intermediates of type A in situ
generated from amino acid-based phosphine and acrylate were
rightfully utilized as organic base catalysts ( Figure 1 a).
However, despite such impressive progress has been made,
important challenges remain. Among them are (1) the
evaluation of the previously unexplored anion moiety of
catalysts, (2) the development of further high e ﬃcient
catalysts, and (3) the extension of the reaction scope.
In this study, we attempted to develop an elegant and
complementary phosphine-containing organic base catalysis
toward meeting these challenges. Indeed, the intrinsic
structural weakness of phosphine-acrylate catalyst A is that
this type of zwitterions inevitably bears a formally rotatable sp
3
C−C bond between the phosphonium cation and carbon
anion, which makes the chiral sca ﬀold much more ﬂexible than
the precatalyst phosphine. To address this issue, a structurally
rigid anion sca ﬀold needs to be introduced during the catalyst
design.
7 We reasonably speculate that allenoate is probably a
promising alternative used as anion sources in combination
with amino acid-based bifunctional phosphine as a precatalyst
because of the following structurally natural advantages of
zwitterions of type B (Figure 1 b). First, this in situ Brønsted
base catalyst ( B) contains a particular π
3
4 anion unit, which
makes that the skeleton of phosphine-allenoate catalyst B is
relatively more rigid than that of phosphine-acrylate catalyst A

and can thus be favorable to stereoinduction in organic
transformations. Second, the double electron-withdrawing
ester groups located in the anion moiety further enhance the
stability and reactivity of the negatively charged active site of
the catalyst. Additionally, the cation moiety of amino acid-
derived phosphines
1 not only possesses remarkably high
tunability but also contains properly installed hydrogen-
bonding donors, which would possibly lead to an enhanced
stereochemical communication between the catalyst and
substrate. With these views in mind, we have identi ﬁed the
allenoate as a particularly promising alternative for new
phosphine-containing organic base catalysis. In the ﬁrst
example, we describe that a su ﬃciently active and unprece-
dentedly stereoselective phosphine-allenoate catalyst enabled
asymmetric construction of N-substituted quaternary stereo-
centers via a decarboxylative addition of cyclic ketimines and
β-keto acids.
This decarboxylative Mannich-type reaction, which mimics
the reaction pathway of natural biosynthesis, was shown to be
one of the most straightforward and e ﬃcient approaches for
producing functionalized chiral amines.
8 The reaction was
typically catalyzed by Lewis acid and chiral amine catalysts, and
important advances have been achieved so far. 9,10 Never-
theless, the asymmetric versions on decarboxylative addition of
sterically hindered ketimines particularly as cyclic N-sulfonyl
ketimines are very rare 9d−g,10a despite the fact that such
process provides a powerful tool for preparing biologically
valuable but synthetically ch allenging N-containing fully
substituted stereocenters, 11 which are also signi ﬁcant building
blocks in numerous bioactive compounds ( Scheme 1 ).12
Furthermore, to the best of our knowledge, there is no report
on an asymmetric decarboxyl ative addition process in
application of phosphine-containing organic base catalysis.
On account of our continuous interest on developing novel
phosphonium-involving organocatalysis, 13 we were fascinated
with the possibility that the aforementioned in situ bifunctional
Brønsted base catalyst of phosphine-allenoate ( B) might
provide su ﬃcient activation for the challenging ketimine
substrates and thus realize a highly stereoselective decarbox-
ylative addition using broad β-keto acids as reaction partners.
Herein, we present a new class of dipeptide-based phosphine-
allenoate catalyst and its ﬁrst application example on catalytic
asymmetric decarboxylative addition reaction between cyclic
ketimines and β-keto acids ( Figure 1 c), thus leading to facile
construction of N-containing fully substituted stereocenter
systems.
■ RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
Asymmetric Decarboxylative Addition of Cyclic
Ketimines with Aryl Substituted β-Keto Acids. Initially,
we selected cyclic N-sulfonyl α-ketimino ester 1a and β-keto
acid 2a as model substrates for optimizing reaction conditions
(Table 1). The reaction was ﬁrst performed in the presence of
a L-Val-D-Val-based bifunctional phosphine catalyst P1 and
allenoate E1 under ambient atmosphere with dichloromethane
as a solvent, and the desired additive product 3a was obtained
in excellent yield (95%) but with disappointing enantiose-
lectivity (3% ee) (entry 1). We were not discouraged by this
result because it still veri ﬁed that the catalytic ability of this

dual system is assured. Later, we examined the combination of
L-Val-L-Val- or L-Val-L-tert-Leu-based phosphine catalysts ( P2
or P3) and allenoate E1. To our delight, both excellent yield
and ee value were achieved (entry 2). Further minor
modiﬁcation of phosphine catalysts could make the enantio-
selectivity to be slightly improved, and P4 was ﬁnally proved to
be the best chiral phosphine (entries 3 and 4). Of note, the
monofunctional phosphine ( S)-BINAP ( P5) was screened to
give the desired product in an almost racemic form, which
implied that the hydrogen-bonding interaction is crucial for
stereocontrol (entry 5). Later, the solvent e ﬀect was evaluated
under the optimized catalyst of P4/E1 combination (entries 6−
9). It was found that diethyl ether showed the highest
performance toward both reactivity and enantioselectivity
(entry 9). By comparison, when acrylate E2 was used as a co-
catalyst alternative for chiral phosphine P4, the reaction worked
and aﬀorded the desired product 3a with low ee (entry 10, see
Table S6 in Supporting Information for details). This result
strongly supported our hypothesis that ﬂexibility of the
phosphine-acrylate catalyst would dramatically decrease the
enantioselectivity. Notably, reducing the catalyst loading to 0.5
mol % could also a ﬀord excellent reaction results (98% yield
and >99.9% ee) (entry 11). Moreover, the racemic product
was formed in the absence of either allenoate E1 or both P4
and E1, which suggested that the in situ generated zwitterion
was the catalytically active species for promoting this
enantioselective decarboxylative addition (entries 12 and 13).
With the optimized reaction conditions identi ﬁed (entry 11,
Table 1 ), a large range of cyclic N-sulfonyl ketimines bearing
diﬀerent substituent groups were investigated. In all cases, the
reaction proceeded smoothly and a ﬀorded the desired product
in good to excellent yields (83 −99%) with unprecedented
enantioselectivities (Table 2). It is worth noting that all desired
products were obtained with very excellent enantioselectivities
(99.0 to >99.9% ee) irrespective of the electronic nature and
positions of substituents. The reactivity of the title reaction is
generally high under phosphine-allenoate catalysis. In the case
of substrates bearing electron-withdrawing groups such as
either F or CF 3 at the 5-position, the yields of desired products
(3g and 3h) were slightly lower than others (entries 7 and 8).
Subsequently, the catalytic system was also examined for the
decarboxylative addition reactions of various aryl-substituted β-
keto acids ( Table 3 ). To our surprise, excellent yields (91 −
98%) with unprecedented stereoselectivities (99.0 to >99.9%
ee) were achieved for all entries. The phosphine-allenoate ( P4/
E1) combination seems to be an “ideal” catalytic system for this
enantioselective chemical process, in which the electronic and
steric e ﬀects of substituents on the aromatic ring have little
inﬂuence on both catalytic reactivity and enantioselectivity
under this dual catalysis. In addition, the malonic acid half
thioester 2t was also a suitable substrate to give the
corresponding adduct 4t in 98% yield with >99% ee under
the standard reaction conditions using dichloromethane as the
solvent alternatively.
Asymmetric Decarboxylative Addition between Cy-
clic Ketimines and Alkyl-Substituted β-Keto Acids.
Compared with aryl-substituted β-keto acids, alkyl-substituted
β-keto acids are less studied in such decarboxylative addition
reactions owing to their intrinsic instability toward most
catalytic environment. The aliphatic β-keto acids have a greater
tendency to undergo the decarboxylative process very rapidly
before and after the desired addition process, which may cause
low e ﬃciency and stereoselectivity. 11c Indeed, while the
decarboxylative addition of 3-oxopentanoic acid 5a with cyclic
ketimine 1a was performed under the above-mentioned
standard conditions, it was found that the yield maintained
with a longer reaction time (24 h), but the enantioselectivity
dropped to 38% ee ( Table 4 , entry 4). To improve the

Scaled-Up Synthesis and Transformations of the
Product. To demonstrate the scalability and the practicality
of the process, scaled-up preparation and synthetic trans-
formations of the product were performed. As shown in
Scheme 2 a, scaled-up reactions of cyclic ketimine 1a with
diﬀerent β-keto acids were performed, and the corresponding
products were isolated in high yields without any loss of ee
values. Furthermore, selective reductions of the title product
3a using either Pd/C or NaBH
4 reagent could a ﬀord di ﬀerent
chiral compounds ( 8 and 9) in high yields and excellent ee
values, respectively. Also, treatment of 3a with TBHP and KI
led to simultaneous cyclization reactions for furnishing the
aziridine compound ((+)- 10), which are prevalent building
blocks in many biologically active compounds.
14 In addition,
the corresponding derivative ( −)-10 was also prepared
(Schemes S1 and S2 ), and the absolute con ﬁguration of the
(−)-10 was assigned to be (1 R,7 bS) by X-ray crystallographic
analysis of its single crystal ( Scheme 3 ).15 Accordingly, the
absolute con ﬁguration of the product (+)- 3a was assigned to
be R, and the absolute con ﬁguration of the product ( −)-3a was
thus assigned to be S.T h ec o n ﬁgurations of other
decarboxylative addition products were accordingly assigned
by analogy.
Mechanistic Insights. The mechanistic reaction cycle of
this decarboxylative addition is also believed to follow the
general mechanism described in the literature,
10,11 and the
detailed reaction pathway is shown in Figure 2 . First, the
nucleophilic addition of phosphine to the electron-de ﬁcient
allenoate generates the zwitterion B,w h i c hc a nf u r t h e r
deprotonate the incoming β-keto acid 2a to form an ion-pair
I that contains the phosphonium intermediate C and the
anionic form of the nucleophile D. Then, addition of D to the
ketimine 1a leads to anionic E which may be stabilized by
phosphonium C (ion-pair II). The intermediate E abstracts a
proton from β-keto acid 2a to generate the key intermediate
In-III by forming the corresponding anionic D which will go
into the reaction cycle again. At last, decarboxylation of the key
intermediate In- III aﬀords the desired product 3a.
To gain a better understanding of this reaction cycle, in situ
NMR and ESI/MS methods were used to study this
decarboxylative addition reaction.

■ CONCLUSIONS
In summary, we have designed and developed a new type of
dipeptide-based in situ phosphonium-containing organocatalyst
and successfully achieved its application in the asymmetric
construction of sterically hindered N-containing fully sub-
stituted stereocenters via an asymmetric decarboxylative
Mannich process between β-keto acids and cyclic ketimines.
In the presence of such a in situ bifunctional Brønsted base
catalyst, the addition reactions proceeded smoothly for a broad
variety of β-keto acids together with numerous cyclic ketimines
under very low catalyst loading (0.5 mol %) and a ﬀorded series
of functionalized tertiary amine-containing cyclic compounds
in high yields with unprecedented enantioselectivities (99.0 to
>99.9% ee). The practicality and the utility of this protocol
were demonstrated by the scale-up synthetic reaction and facile
elaborations. In addition, mechanistic investigations indicate
that the reaction proceeds via a stepwise process of
nucleophilic addition and subsequent decarboxylation. Further
developments and applications of this novel in situ bifunctional
phosphonium-containing organocatalyst to other challenging
areas of organic synthesis are currently ongoing in our
laboratory.
